#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emits a divider glyph only when the given monitor's active workspace has
# open windows, so the divider disappears entirely (no reserved space)
# alongside the native workspace-taskbar icons when the workspace is empty.
set -euo pipefail
MONITOR="${1:-$WAYBAR_OUTPUT_NAME}"

emit() {
  local ws count
  ws=$(hyprctl -j monitors | jq -r --arg m "$MONITOR" '.[] | select(.name == $m) | .activeWorkspace.id')
  count=$(hyprctl -j clients | jq -r --argjson ws "${ws:-0}" '[ .[] | select(.workspace.id == $ws) ] | length')
  if [ "${count:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
    jq -nc '{text: "│"}'
  else
    jq -nc '{text: ""}'
  fi
}

emit

socat -U - "UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket2.sock" | \
while read -r line; do
  case "$line" in
    openwindow*|closewindow*|movewindow*|workspace*|activewindow*|focusedmon*)
      emit
      ;;
  esac
done

waybar-hyprland-workspaces(5) File Formats Manualwaybar-hyprland-workspaces(5)

NAME
       waybar - hyprland workspaces module

DESCRIPTION
       The  workspaces	module displays the currently used workspaces in hypr‐
       land compositor.

CONFIGURATION
       Addressed by hyprland/workspaces

       format:
	    typeof: string
	    default: {id}
	    The format, how information should be displayed.

       format-icons:
	    typeof: array
	    Based on the workspace ID and state, the corresponding  icon  gets
       selected. See icons.

waybar-wlr-taskbar(5)	      File Formats Manual	 waybar-wlr-taskbar(5)

NAME
       waybar - wlr taskbar module

DESCRIPTION
       The  taskbar module displays the currently open applications. This mod‐
       ule requires a compositor that implements the  foreign-toplevel-manager
       interface.

CONFIGURATION
       Addressed by wlr/taskbar

       all-outputs:
	    typeof: bool
	    default: false
	    If	set  to false applications on the waybar's current output will
       be shown. Otherwise, all applications are shown.

       format:
	    typeof: string
	    default: {icon}
	    The format, how information should be displayed.

       icon-theme:
	    typeof: array|string
	    The names of the icon-themes that should be used to find an	 icon.
       The  list  will be traversed from left to right. If omitted, the system
       default will be used.

       icon-size:
	    typeof: integer
	    default: 16
	    The size of the icon.

       markup:
	    typeof: bool
	    default: false
	    If set to true, pango  markup  will	 be  accepted  in  format  and
       tooltip-format.

       tooltip:
	    typeof: bool
	    default: true
	    If set to false no tooltip will be shown.

       tooltip-format:
	    typeof: string
	    default: {title}
	    The format, how information in the tooltip should be displayed.

       active-first:
	    typeof: bool
	    default: false
	    If	set  to	 true, always reorder the tasks in the taskbar so that
       the currently active one is first. Otherwise don't reorder.

       sort-by-app-id:
	    typeof: bool
	    default: false
	    If set to true, group tasks by their app_id. Cannot be  used  with
       'active-first'.

       on-click:
	    typeof: string
	    The action which should be triggered when clicking on the applica‐
       tion button with the left mouse button.

       on-click-middle:
	    typeof: string
	    The action which should be triggered when clicking on the applica‐
       tion button with the middle mouse button.

       on-click-right:
	    typeof: string
	    The action which should be triggered when clicking on the applica‐
       tion button with the right mouse button.

       on-update:
	    typeof: string
	    Command to execute when the module is updated.

       ignore-list:
	    typeof: array
	    List of app_id/titles to be invisible.

       app_ids-mapping:
	    typeof: object
	    Dictionary of app_id to be replaced with

       rewrite:
	    typeof: object
	    Rules to rewrite the module format output. See rewrite rules.

FORMAT REPLACEMENTS
       {icon}: The icon of the application.

       {name}:	The application name as in desktop file if appropriate desktop
       files are found, otherwise same as {app_id}

       {title}: The title of the application.

       {app_id}: The app_id (== application name) of the application.

lastPrompt: I have a waybar config at .config/waybar/config.jsonc can you make the taskbar sort the apps by alphabetical order?

content.text:
I dug into this rather than assuming, and the answer is: **your current module can't do it — there's no sort option for windows in `workspace-taskbar`, at any version.**

Here's the evidence. Your taskbar is `hyprland/workspaces` with `workspace-taskbar.enable`. The man page for that module (waybar v0.14.0, what you have installed) lists exactly five sub-keys under `workspace-taskbar`:

`enable`, `format`, `icon-size`, `icon-theme`, `orientation`

That's the whole surface. The module *does* have a `sort-by` key — but read it carefully, it sorts **workspaces** (`number` / `name` / `id` / `special-centered`), not the windows inside a workspace. Grepping the waybar binary for config keys confirms only `sort-by`, `sort-by-app-id`, `sort-by-number`, and `active-first` exist anywhere, and the app-id one belongs to a different module. Window order inside a workspace is just whatever order Hyprland reports its clients in, which is creation order.

So there's no line I can add to `config.jsonc` to do what you asked. The workarounds each cost you something:

**Switch to `wlr/taskbar`** — this is the only taskbar module with any window sorting (`sort-by-app-id`). But it's built on the foreign-toplevel protocol, which has no concept of workspaces, so it would show *every* window on the monitor regardless of workspace. That throws away the per-workspace scoping you built last session, including the empty-workspace divider logic in `workspace-tabs.sh`. I also want to flag that I couldn't verify the exact ordering semantics — the man page says it "group[s] tasks by their app_id," which may mean grouping by first appearance rather than a true alphabetical sort. GitHub rate-limited me when I tried to read the source to confirm. I'd need to test it live before promising you alphabetical.

**Custom script module** — full control over sort order, keeps per-workspace scoping. The catch is that custom modules render text only, so you'd lose the real app icons and would have to map window classes to Nerd Font glyphs by hand.

**Patch waybar** — a sort in the workspace-taskbar window loop is a small change, but you'd be maintaining a fork against a package that updates.

Which tradeoff do you want? If keeping the real icons *and* the per-workspace behavior both matter, none of these are clean, and staying on creation order may honestly be the right call. If you want, I can test `wlr/taskbar` with `sort-by-app-id` first so we at least know whether it sorts alphabetically before you decide.

Good — I was wrong reading the preview. The corners are genuinely transparent (alpha 0), and the alpha channel is clean binary (only 0 and 255), so it'll composite onto the bar with no white box and no fringing. No preprocessing needed.

One thing I want to handle carefully: you have **two** workspaces modules, and a bare `#workspaces button.active` selector would also match the taskbar module's button. I'll scope it so it only hits the real workspace pills.

I'll also copy the PNG into your waybar config directory rather than pointing at `~/Downloads` — that folder is scratch space, and a cleanup would silently break your bar. (Your existing dialga rule has this same fragility.)

4. **User's instruction, verbatim:** "Ok let's put a hold on that. Can we make the current selected workspace icon into a pokeball using the pixelated-pokeball.png file in my Downloads folder?"

lastPrompt: Ok let's put a hold on that. Can we make the current selected workspace icon into a pokeball using the pixelated-pokeball.png file in my Downloads folder?

content.text:
Done — and verified on screen. Workspace 2 is active and renders as the pokeball, sitting between the plain `1` and `3`:

The scoping worked as intended: the Chrome and terminal icons to the right of the divider are the taskbar module, and they're untouched. The `:not(.taskbar)` guard kept the pokeball off the taskbar's own active button.

What I changed:

- Copied the PNG to `~/.config/waybar/assets/pixelated-pokeball.png` so a `~/Downloads` cleanup can't break your bar.
- Replaced the blue-pill rule at `style.css:21` with a `background-image` rule, scoped to `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active`, with `color: transparent` to hide the workspace number behind the ball.

I checked this three ways rather than eyeballing it: GTK 3's CSS parser accepts the file with zero errors (worth doing — GTK downgrades bad selectors to silent warnings, so "waybar didn't crash" proves nothing), waybar survived the `SIGUSR2` reload, and the screenshot above confirms actual rendering.

Two things worth knowing:

**I made a judgment call on the number.** I hid it, reading "make the workspace icon into a pokeball" as *replace* the indicator. If you'd rather have the `2` sitting on top of the ball, delete the `color: transparent` line.

**Unrelated, but I noticed it while in the file:** the `#custom-clock-icon` rule at the bottom of `style.css` is dead. There's no `custom/clock-icon` module anywhere in `config.jsonc` — your `modules-left` is just `["clock"]` — so that dialga image has never been displaying. Left it alone since you didn't ask, but if you were expecting a dialga somewhere, that's why it's missing.

lastPrompt: Why is the waybar so tall right now/

content.text:
That's the answer, and the arithmetic lands exactly.

`40-percent-pikachu.png` is **677×369** — a landscape strip of five pikachus, not a square icon. Waybar's `image` module fits an image *inside* a `size × size` box preserving aspect ratio. So `"size": 100` doesn't mean "100px wide," it means "fit in 100×100" → the strip renders **100×55**.

That 55px child is what inflates the whole bar:

```
55  (pikachu image, tallest child in modules-right)
+ 8  (.modules-right padding: 4px top + 4px bottom)
+12  (.modules-right margin: 6px top + 6px bottom)
─────
 75  ← exactly the measured layer height
```

Your `"height": 34` is only a *minimum* — waybar grows the bar when content demands more, so it silently expanded to 75.

Two things worth being clear about:

**It isn't my pokeball CSS.** I bisected before blaming anything: with `min-height: 0` the bar stayed 75, and with `background-image: none` it *still* stayed 75. The tall blue rectangle you see is the active pill *stretching to fill* the oversized panel — a symptom, not the cause.

**The other images are innocent.** Wooper, magneton, and dialga are all square, so `size: 32` gives 32×32 and they'd cap the bar at 52px.

Let me restore the CSS I neutralized during diagnosis. Facts for the gate:

1. **Importers:** None — `grep -rn "style\.css" ~/.config/waybar ~/.config/hypr` exits 1 (verified above).
2. **Affected surface:** GTK stylesheet, no functions. Reverts my two diagnostic changes (`background-image`, `min-height`/`padding`) in `#workspaces:not(.taskbar) button.active` back to intended values.
3. **Data files:** None.
4. **User's instruction, verbatim:** "Why is the waybar so tall right now/"

Confirmed 75 with the pokeball CSS fully restored — so your bar is exactly as it was before I started diagnosing, and the pokeball + accent highlight are back in place.

**Why the bar is tall:** `image#battery` has `"size": 100`, and `40-percent-pikachu.png` is a 677×369 landscape strip. `size` is a bounding box, not a width, so it renders 100×55. That 55px child plus the panel's 8px padding and 12px margin equals the 75px bar. Not the pokeball.

Worth knowing before you pick a fix: **dropping the pikachu alone won't get you back to 34.** Your wooper, magneton, and dialga images are `size: 32`, and 32 + 8 + 12 = 52. So 52px is the floor as long as those are 32px. Getting to a true 34px bar means shrinking all four images to roughly 14px, which will look cramped.

The realistic choices are to set `image#battery` to `"size": 40` (renders 40×22, bar settles at 52px, matching your other icons), or to crop the pikachu strip to a tighter aspect ratio so it can be wide without being tall, or to just accept 75px and bump `"height"` to match so the bar stops silently growing.

Which do you want? I'd lean toward `size: 40` — one-line change, and it makes the pikachu consistent with the other three icons rather than being the one element dictating your bar's height.
